calls.head: The Penguins want Lapierre away from the big guns
calls.body: At home, the Penguins keep sending Lapierre’s line (McGroarty, Lapierre and Koivunen) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Dan Muse has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Suniev, Castagna and Tsyplakov.

surprises.head: Calgary’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Calgary has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 0.0 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 6.5 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Farabee has a goal and an assist as the Flames take down the Penguins
paras: Tommy Novak struck first for the Penguins late in the first. The Flames scored four times in the second. Joel Farabee made it 1-1 for Calgary just 38 seconds into the second, and Brennan Othmann put the Flames ahead 2-1 early in the period. Maxim Tsyplakov scored his first goal for Calgary a little over four minutes later to make it 3-1. Evgeni Malkin pulled the Penguins within one on the power play a little over four minutes later. Ryan Strome extended the lead to 4-2, 21 seconds later. Rickard Rakell pulled the Pens within one on the power play 43 seconds later, but they got no closer. Jonathan Castagna made it 5-3 for the Flames midway through the third. Yegor Sharangovich added an empty-net goal with a little over two minutes left to make it 6-3.

The Penguins had a little more of the play, but the Flames made their chances count. Dustin Wolf made 25 saves for the Flames, and Artūrs Šilovs allowed five goals on 26 shots. The Flames moved to 11-13-2 and climbed to fourth in the Pacific, while the Penguins dropped to 7-15-2, still last in the Metropolitan.
